newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - England heading for victory vs NZ XI.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - England heading for victory vs NZ XI.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Jan 16 - England were heading for victory at lunch on the final day of their first-class cricket tour match against the New Zealand Selection XI on Thursday.
At lunch the Selection XI were 100 for seven wickets in their second innings, still trailing England by 189 runs with two sessions left in the match.
Llorne Howell was not out on nine and Mark Haslam had yet to score.
The Selection XI began the day at 25-1, aiming to bat through the day to save the match.
However, Adam Parore was out inside the first hour, caught behind off fast-medium Chris Silverwood for 13. Wickets then fell steadily, three falling at one point in the space of 22 balls.

Matt Horne was snapped up at silly point off left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell; Mark Greatbatch, after thumping a six and a four from Tufnell, was run out by a direct throw from mid off, and Justin Vaughan was caught at second slip off Silverwood.
Opener Blair Pocock had grafted 189 minutes and faced 143 balls over his 43 before trying to sweep Tufnell.
The ball lobbed over wicketkeeper Alec Stewart and Nasser Hussain dived forward at slip to take a good catch.
Paul Wiseman shouldered arms and went leg-before-wicket to Tufnell for his second duck of the match, just before the interval.
Tufnell had taken 3-20 from 14 overs and Silverwood 2-24 from 13.
